arxiv-1701-04786.title: On Higher-Order Probabilistic Subrecursion
arxiv-1701-04786.creator: Flavien Breuvart, Ugo Dal Lago, Agathe Herrou
arxiv-1701-04786.description: Abstract . We study the expressive power of subrecursive probabilistic higher-order calculi. More specifically, we show that endowing a very expressive deterministic calculus like Gödel’s 𝕋 \mathbb{T} with various forms of probabilistic choice operators may result in calculi which are not equivalent as for the class of distributions they give rise to, although they all guarantee almost-sure termination.

arxiv-2201-08746.title: ERS: a novel comprehensive endoscopy image dataset for machine learning, compliant with the MST 3.0 specification
arxiv-2201-08746.creator: Jan Cychnerski, Tomasz Dziubich, Adam Brzeski
arxiv-2201-08746.description: Abstract The article presents a new multi-label comprehensive image dataset from flexible endoscopy, colonoscopy and capsule endoscopy, named ERS. The collection has been labeled according to the full medical specification of ’Minimum Standard Terminology 3.0’ (MST 3.0), describing all possible findings in the gastrointestinal tract (104 possible labels), extended with an additional 19 labels useful in common machine learning applications.

arxiv-2310-17518.creator: Nouredine Medjoudj, Abdelkrim Moussaoui
arxiv-2310-17518.description: Abstract . We establish the existence and uniqueness of solutions for quasilinear singular Lane-Emden type systems subjected to Neumann boundary conditions. arxiv-2410-19498.title: Assessment of Abrupt Shifts in CMIP6 Models using Edge Detection
arxiv-2410-19498.creator: Sjoerd Terpstra, Swinda K.J. Falkena, Robbin Bastiaansen, Sebastian Bathiany, Henk A. Dijkstra, Anna S. von der Heydt
arxiv-2410-19498.description: Abstract Research over the past decade has shown that multiple elements of the climate system, such as the Arctic Winter sea ice or the Amazon rainforest, could undergo abrupt shifts, but there are large uncertainties regarding their timing and spatial extent.

arxiv-2502-19810.title: Automatic Linear Resource Bound Analysis for Rust via Prophecy Potentials
arxiv-2502-19810.creator: Qihao Lian, Di Wang
arxiv-2502-19810.description: Abstract . Rust has become a popular system programming language that strikes a balance between memory safety and performance. Rust’s type system ensures the safety of low-level memory controls; however, a well-typed Rust program is not guaranteed to enjoy high performance. This article studies static analysis for resource consumption of Rust programs, aiming at understanding the performance of Rust programs.

arxiv-2512-04042.creator: Richard Ignace, Christiana Erba, Kaylee DeGennaro, Gary D. Henson

arxiv-2512-20347.title: Three-dimensional mesh adaptation in PFEM Preprint
arxiv-2512-20347.creator: Thomas Leyssens, Jonathan Lambrechts, Jean-François Remacle
arxiv-2512-20347.description: Abstract Chaotic free surface flows are challenging problems to simulate numerically, mainly due to the significant changes in geometry and frequent topological changes. Methods that track the evolution of the fluid in a Lagrangian formulation are a natural choice. One such method is the Particle Finite Element Method (PFEM).

pmc-10519946.title: Case analysis of long-term negative psychological responses to psychedelics
pmc-10519946.creator: Rebecka Bremler, Nancy Katati, Parvinder Shergill, David Erritzoe, Robin L. Carhart-Harris
pmc-10519946.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Recent controversies have arisen regarding claims of uncritical positive regard and hype surrounding psychedelic drugs and their therapeutic potential. Criticisms have included that study designs and reporting styles bias positive over negative outcomes. The present study was motivated by a desire to address this alleged bias by intentionally focusing exclusively on negative outcomes, defined as self-perceived ‘negative’ psychological responses lasting for at least 72 h after psychedelic use.

pmc-10627555.title: DNA Sequences Are as Useful as Protein Sequences for Inferring Deep Phylogenies
pmc-10627555.creator: Paschalia Kapli, Ioanna Kotari, Maximilian J Telford, Nick Goldman, Ziheng Yang, Lars Jermiin
pmc-10627555.description: Inference of deep phylogenies has almost exclusively used protein rather than DNA sequences based on the perception that protein sequences are less prone to homoplasy and saturation or to issues of compositional heterogeneity than DNA sequences. Here, we analyze a model of codon evolution under an idealized genetic code and demonstrate that those perceptions may be misconceptions.

pmc-11339402.title: Immune killer cells treatment for previously treated stage IV NSCLC patients
pmc-11339402.creator: Yen-Han Tseng, Ching-Liang Ho, Chih-Feng Chian, Chi-Lu Chiang, Heng-Sheng Chao, Chen-Liang Tsai, Wann-Cherng Perng, Chin-Fu Hsiao, Mei-Hsing Chuang, Kai-Hsiung Ko, Yun-Ching Cheng, Shin-Jung Chen, Chia-Jen Wang, Yuh-Min Chen
pmc-11339402.description: The 5-year survival is poor for stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Recently, cell immunotherapy has emerged as a new treatment strategy. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Immune killer cells (IKC) in patients with stage IV NSCLC after the failure of prior chemotherapy.

pmc-11450802.title: Electricity-driven organic hydrogenation using water as the hydrogen source
pmc-11450802.creator: Bidyut Kumar Kundu, Yujie Sun
pmc-11450802.description: Hydrogenation is a pivotal process in organic synthesis and various catalytic strategies have been developed in achieving effective hydrogenation of diverse substrates. Despite the competence of these methods, the predominant reliance on molecular hydrogen (H2) gas under high temperature and elevated pressure presents operational challenges.

pmc-11679672.title: Upcity: Addressing Urban Problems Through an Integrated System
pmc-11679672.creator: Andre A F Silva, Adao J S Porto, Bruno M C Belo, Cecilia A C Cesar, Maurizio Mongelli, Jerome Guzzi
pmc-11679672.description: Current technologies could potentially solve many of the urban problems in today’s cities. Many cities already possess cameras, drones, thermometers, pollution air gauges, and other sensors. However, most of these have been designated for use in individual domains within City Hall, creating a maze of individual data domains that cannot connect to each other.

pmc-12590099.title: Disease Burden and Sexual Life in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: A Phenomenological Study
pmc-12590099.creator: Seher Çakmak, Sevda Uzun, Sevgi Demir Çam
pmc-12590099.description: This study aims to examine the burden of disease experienced by multiple sclerosis patients and to deeply examine the impact of the disease on sexual life. A phenomenological research design was used in this study. This qualitative research was conducted with 20 multiple sclerosis patients. Interviews were conducted individually and face‐to‐face. The data were analyzed using Colaizzi's phenomenological analysis method.

pmc-12716547.title: Prevalence, determinants and ethnic disparities of rheumatoid arthritis among older adults in Canada: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12716547.creator: Lakew Mussie, G Mutwiri, Amanuel Yoseph
pmc-12716547.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). AbstractIntroductionRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterised by progressive joint inflammation, pain and functional decline, disproportionately affecting older adults. In Canada, evidence regarding the prevalence, determinants and ethnic disparities of RA among older populations remains fragmented.

pmc-13136858.title: Biological Degradation of Spent Coffee Grounds by White Rot Fungi
pmc-13136858.creator: Anna Civzele, Anna Sila, Linda Mezule
pmc-13136858.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Spent coffee grounds (SCG) are extensively generated as a byproduct of coffee production and consumption. Improper disposal of SCG contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, environmental pollution, and the loss of valuable resources when landfilled or discharged into sewage systems. In response, this study investigates the biodegradation potential of SCG using selected wood‐decay fungi known for their ability to secrete a wide spectrum of lignocellulose‐degrading enzymes and degrade complex organic compounds.
